Raises

Raises - Universal Combat Raise Catalog

One Raise catalog for every delivery. Martial and Spell attacks use the same Raise values.

  1. Before rolling, declare the number of Paid Raises. Each Paid Raise adds +4 to the applicable Target Number. This is the sole success TN for the attack or affected target.
  2. Roll against the raised TN. An AoE uses one roll and checks each target separately. A Power creating an area without an immediate target checks its printed base TN plus the Paid Raises.
  3. After resolving the roll, assign each successful Raise to one of the two options below. Apply the chosen effects before Damage and Specials resolve. A Raise may only modify a property the Power already has.
Raises spent Universal effect
1 Add +MR d8 Damage to the Power's existing Damage Roll. For an AoE, add +ceil(MR / 2) d8 instead (round the number of bonus dice up).
1 Add +MR to one existing numeric Special(X) applied by the Power.

Multiple Raises may be assigned to the same option. Range, Melee Reach, AoE size, and Duration use the Power's printed values and do not change through combat Raises. This keeps target declaration and Attack-Trigger Reactions in the normal pre-roll window.

Split Attack: One Power use makes up to two separate Attack or Casting Rolls using its divided Pool. Declare one Paid Raise count for the Power; add the same TN increase to both rolls. After resolving both rolls, choose the Raise effects once and apply that same choice to each successful split. Each successful split deals full Damage and its full Special payload. The split rolls determine hits independently.

Intellect Free Raises: Declare how many of the current Round's allowance are committed to this use before rolling. They use the same two options without raising TN, and are consumed as described by the Stone Ability. For Split Attack, commit them once for the Power, not separately for each split.

Example: At MR3 a character declares one Paid Raise against TN22, making the new TN26. A roll of 25 fails; a roll of 28 succeeds. After success, the player chooses +3d8 Damage, +2d8 Damage if the Power is AoE, or +3 to an existing numeric Special. Martial and Spell use the same values.

Round Structure

Round Structure

Each combat follows this structure:

  1. Preparation Phase The Preparation Phase takes place before the Round begins. Creatures prepare Stone Abilities and choose any Active Buff activation or replacement before any Turn. Round-based benefits apply throughout the upcoming Round, regardless of Initiative Order.

    • At the start of this Phase, first receive Ready Absorption Stones earned through eligible Scarred Health Bars since the previous Preparation Phase.
    • On the first Round only, roll Initiative.
    • Before any creature moves, acts, or begins its Turn, all creatures prepare their Stone use for the Round.
    • Resolve Initiative Boost first. Any Stones used for Initiative Boost are committed and spent immediately.
    • Resolve Initiative Exchange and convert Initiative into Initiative Colorless Stones.
    • After Initiative Exchange, creatures commit and spend their remaining Ready Stones and any Initiative Colorless Stones on their other Stone Abilities for the Round.
    • Defensive and passive Stone values that apply during the Round become active immediately.
    • Stone Abilities with a Turn timing or trigger are prepared now but resolve at their specified time.
    • Activate, keep, or replace an Active Buff here. A new activation commits this Round's base Attack Action. Apply any Active Buff Empowerment chosen in this same Phase and initialize Buff resources once.
    • Once Preparation choices are complete, determine Initiative Order and lock it for this Round.

  2. Resolve Turns

    • Creatures act in Initiative Order.
    • Each creature takes one Turn per Round.

  3. End the Round

    • Resolve end-of-round effects.
    • Expire Round-based Stone Ability effects, unused Round-based pools, and Active Buffs reaching their final Round End.
    • Recover Exhausted Stones according to normal Stone Recovery.

  4. Start a New Round

    • Keep all remaining Initiative Scores.
    • Begin a new Preparation Phase.
    • Do not roll Initiative again unless a rule explicitly allows it.

Basic Action Kit

At the start of each Round, each character normally has:

  • 1 Movement
  • 1 Attack Action
  • 1 Reaction

Some Powers, Items, or Stones may grant additional Movements, Attack Actions, or Reactions. A base Attack Action committed to an Active Buff in Preparation is unavailable on that Round's Turn; legal additional Attack Actions remain usable.

::

Turn Structure

On your Turn, resolve the following steps in order:

  1. Start of Turn
  2. Movement and Attack Action
  3. End of Turn

Start of Turn

At the start of your Turn, resolve all effects that trigger at the start of your Turn.

This includes:

  • ongoing damage,
  • Diminishing Stack ticks,
  • start-of-turn buffs,
  • start-of-turn penalties,
  • and similar effects.

Resolve effects at the start of your Turn in this order:

  1. Resolve Ticks of Diminishing Specials already present when this Turn began (for example, existing Ruin and Slow).
  2. Apply Natural Special Recovery to eligible negative Diminishing Specials.
  3. Apply normal Diminishing Decay of −1 to each stored Diminishing stack. Resolve Root's separate start-of-turn reduction by the affected creature's MR.
  4. Apply legal start-of-turn benefits, including Passive: Self Cleanse (additional to Natural Special Recovery), Active Buff: Self Cleanse, and eligible healing. Active Buff: Temporary HP refreshes in Preparation, not here.
  5. Resolve Persistent Zone start-of-turn applications for zones the creature is currently inside. Newly applied Specials enter the active stacks now; their first normal start-of-turn Tick occurs at the creature's next eligible Turn start.

A Persistent Zone also applies when it appears around a creature or the creature first enters it during a Round, according to the zone's normal rules. Each zone/creature pair makes at most one application attempt per Round, including an application resisted by Spell Resistance. Once attempted, further entry or start-of-turn events in that Round do not cause another application from that zone.

Root does not receive Natural Special Recovery or Diminishing Decay. Its own start-of-turn MR reduction is resolved in Step 3. Negative special Tick damage remains governed by its own mitigation rules.

Example:

Ruin(4) resolves its Tick, may be reduced by Natural Special Recovery, and then decays by 1. Diminishing Specials cannot decay below 0.

Movement and Attack Action

During your Turn, you may use:

  • 1 Movement
  • 1 Attack Action

You may use them in either order unless a rule says otherwise. A Movement may be normal Movement or a Movement Power. An available Attack Action may be used to:

  • make a weapon attack,
  • use an Active Power,
  • cast a Spell,
  • use an item,
  • or perform another action that costs an Attack Action.

Active Buffs activate only in Preparation, never through a Turn Attack Action.

Reactions

A Reaction is used when its specific Trigger occurs. You normally have 1 Reaction per Round. Additional Reactions may be spent when an eligible Trigger occurs.

Reaction Trigger Windows

Trigger Resolution window
Attack Trigger After the attack, its target or affected area, and its delivery are declared; before the Attack Roll or Casting Roll.
Hit Trigger After a hit is confirmed; before Phasing, Specials, or damage from that hit are resolved.
Damage Trigger After the Damage Roll is known; before Armor, Damage Reduction, Temporary HP, and Health are applied.
Incoming Effect Trigger After Special Negation has reduced an incoming Special; immediately before the remaining Special takes effect.
Ongoing Effect Trigger Immediately before an existing Special's next tick or other effect resolves.

An Ally Trigger uses the same window when that event affects the ally. A Reaction with a more specific printed Trigger uses its printed moment; for example, Reaction: Absorption Surge triggers after an eligible Health Bar becomes Scarred. The Reaction's effect is resolved at that window, unless its text specifies a later resolution.

End of Turn

At the end of your Turn, resolve effects that trigger at the end of your Turn.

Health & Fear

Health & Fear

Damage does not only bring a character closer to defeat.
It also reduces how much of their full potential they can still bring into a roll.

Your Vitality determines the size of your Health Bars.
Each Health Bar represents a deeper stage of injury.

Determining Health Bars

By default, everyone has five Health Bars.

Each Health Bar has:

Vitality × 4 boxes by default. Passive: Fortitude may increase that multiplier to ×5, ×6, ×7, or ×8 at Power Levels 4, 8, 12, and 16, respectively, while slotted. It changes the maximum size of normal Health Bars only; it does not create additional bars, heal lost HP, or reopen Scarred bars. Passive: Health and Passive: Fortitude share the Health category and cannot be slotted together. Passive: Absorption does not grant HP.

After all available Health Bars are depleted (including any additional Bars granted by Growth or other approved effects), the character enters the Incapacitated state, which is represented by one final box.

  • Active Health Bar: the highest Health Bar that is not Scarred.
  • You can heal damage only within your current Active Health Bar.
  • Once a Health Bar is completely filled, it becomes Scarred.
  • A Scarred Health Bar cannot be healed during the same combat unless a rule explicitly allows it.
  • The final box is always Incapacitated.

Health Penalties

Health penalties reduce the number of dice you roll.

Health Healthy Bruised Injured Wounded Broken Incap.
Pool — −10% −20% −40% −50% no actions

Round dice loss down, minimum 0.

Applies to attacks, Attribute Checks, Skill Checks, spells, rituals, and initiative.
Does not reduce damage dice unless a rule explicitly says so.

Order of Pool Reduction

When multiple rules modify a dice pool, apply them in this order:

  1. Start with the relevant Attribute.
  2. Apply Skill training rules.
    • If the Skill is trained enough, use the full Attribute pool.
    • If the Skill is too low, use half the Attribute pool, rounded down.
  3. Apply all flat pool changes from range, environment, Powers, Stones, Buffs, Specials, Fear, or other effects. This includes Weaken, Soulburn, and a subtraction of 1 die for each point of Fear.
  4. Apply the current percentage-based Health Penalty to the remaining pool.
  5. Round the number of dice lost to the Health Penalty down.
  6. Reduce the final Pool no lower than 0 dice. A Pool of 0 fails automatically.
  7. Roll the remaining dice and keep up to Mastery Rank dice (or all of them if fewer remain), unless a rule explicitly modifies Keep.

Flat pool reductions, including accumulated Fear, are applied before the percentage-based Health Penalty. If multiple flat reductions apply to the same roll, add them together before calculating the Health Penalty. Fear reduces Attribute-based roll pools, not Damage Dice or the Mastery-Rank-based Initiative dice; it never reduces Keep.

Example

Someone with Vitality 2 has the following Health Levels.

Each normal Health Bar has:

Vitality × 4 = 8 boxes

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Healthy [Vitality × 4] (No penalty)

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Bruised [Vitality × 4] (−10% dice pool)

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Injured [Vitality × 4] (−20% dice pool)

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Wounded [Vitality × 4] (−40% dice pool)

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Broken [Vitality × 4] (−50% dice pool)

[ ] - Incapacitated

Pool Reduction Example

A character has Agility 16, Mastery Rank 3, and is making a Stealth check. Their Stealth Skill is high enough to use the full Attribute Pool, but they are affected by Weaken(4) and are currently Injured.

  1. Attribute Pool = 16
  2. Skill trained enough → full pool = 16
  3. Weaken(4) removes 4 dice → 12 dice remain
  4. Injured Health Penalty removes 20% of 12 → lose 2 dice
  5. Final Pool = 10k3

If the same character were Wounded, the 40% Health Penalty would remove 4 dice from the post-Weaken pool of 12.

Final Pool = 8k3

Healing and Scarred-Bar Restoration

Healing has two distinct jobs: restore HP in the current active Health Bar or return a lost Scarred Health Bar to full strength. Each job has its own source and resource.

  • HP Healing: Resolve Stone Ability: Healing heals Self or one ally with 4d8 / 8d8 / 12d8 / 16d8 at Ranks 1-4, within 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 m. Damage Transfer heals its user by actual HP removed from an enemy. End-of-combat and rest recovery refill HP at their stated times.
  • Current Bar: Ordinary HP Healing fills the current active Bar up to its maximum. A living Incapacitated or Stable character who receives positive legal HP Healing reopens Broken and places those HP there, as detailed under Incapacitation & Death.
  • Restoring Scarred Bars: Restoration Actives, Passive: Regeneration (Self), Vitality: Remove Scar, and specified natural, ritual or Artifact effects return Scarred Bars unscarred and at full current HP. Each source spends its printed Scarred-Bar resource. Partially damaged, already available Bars retain their existing HP; damage stays on the Bar where it occurred.
  • Recovery order: Recover the lowest eligible Scarred Bar first, progressing toward Healthy. Recover Broken first when an Incapacitated character needs an available Bar. A specific recovery rule, such as a hidden Growth Bar rule, may specify a different eligible choice. Recalculate the highest available Bar and all applicable Health penalties after recovery.
  • Resource cycles: Each Restoration Power has one finite pool per Safe Haven Rest; several uses draw from that same pool. Regeneration spends its own Self-only allowance per Tyhran Day. A Safe Haven Rest itself naturally returns exactly one Scarred Bar, independently of any Restoration Points the player later chooses to spend.

Restoration works with whole Bars and their full HP capacity; Resolve Healing works with rolled HP and the current Bar. Consult Actives and Passives for the level tables, legal targets and action timing.

Incapacitation & Death

When all of your Health Bars are fully depleted, your body collapses under the weight of battle.

You are now Incapacitated.

Incapacitated

  • You fall Prone.
  • You cannot take Attack Actions, Reactions, or Movement.
  • You begin with 0 Death Marks.
  • At the end of each of your turns, the GM rolls your Death Check. (The roll may be kept secret for dramatic effect.)

Death Check

Use the higher of your Vitality or Resolve.

Roll dice equal to that Attribute and keep dice equal to your Mastery Rank.

Death Check TN = (8 × your Mastery Rank) − 2

A Death Check is a special Attribute Check.

  • Skill Points cannot be spent on it.
  • Vitality cannot be spent after the roll.
  • Health penalties do not reduce the Death Check Pool.
  • Fear does not reduce the Death Check Pool.
  • Only an effect that explicitly modifies Death Checks can change the result.
Result Effect
Success You remain Incapacitated and mark 1 Success.
Failure You gain 1 Death Mark (Failure).

Track both Successes and Death Marks separately:

  • At 4 Successes, you are Stabilized.
  • At 4 Death Marks, you die.

Stabilized

Once 4 Successes are reached or an ally stabilizes you, you are Stable.

  • You remain Unconscious at 0 Health Bars.
  • You no longer roll Death Checks.
  • You remain at 0 boxes and do not awaken until healing or recovery restores you.
  • Positive legal HP Healing or external Scarred-Bar Restoration that creates an available Bar with positive HP awakens you immediately; ordinary stabilization by itself does not.
A living **Incapacitated or Stable** character who receives **positive HP Healing from Resolve or another explicitly permitted HP-healing exception** immediately reopens **Broken**, applies that healing there and regains consciousness with positive HP; this works before stabilization. **External Restoration** can instead fully restore the required Scarred Bar (Broken first), ending Incapacitated/Stable when positive available HP is present. Passive Regeneration cannot be consciously activated by an Incapacitated creature. Neither operation revives a truly Dead creature. Incapacitated ends as soon as the creature has legal available HP again; the Death Check/Success/Death Mark tally for that incapacitation ends. A later incapacitation begins a new tally.

Healing & Assistance

An adjacent ally may:

  • Spend 1 Attack Action to make a Medicine Skill Check against a Difficult TN based on the patient’s Mastery Rank (TN = (12 × MR) − 2). On success, the patient is Stabilized (counts as 4 Successes).
  • Use legally prepared Resolve Stone Healing or a specifically allowed HP-healing exception to restore positive HP; alternatively use a legal external Restoration Active to fully restore Scarred Bars and regain positive available HP.
  • Passive: Regeneration is a conscious Self-only choice for a capable creature; while Incapacitated, recovery comes from an eligible external source.

When light touches flesh, even the dying remember what it means to breathe.

Falling Damage

A creature takes 1d8 Damage for every full 4 m fallen.

Distance Damage
0–3 m —
4–7 m 1d8
8–11 m 2d8
12–15 m 3d8
16–19 m 4d8

Continue this progression for greater distances.

Falling Damage ignores Armor.

Fear

Fear is an accumulating value that starts at 0. When an event or the GM calls for a Fear Check, each selected character rolls their Resolve Pool, keeping one die (Resolve k1). Use the same fixed result bands for ordinary, extreme and supernatural events. The GM chooses who is affected; the band is determined by the roll rather than Challenge MR or an adjustable Difficulty.

Resolve k1 result Fear gained
0-7 +2 Fear
8-15 +1 Fear
16 or higher +0 Fear

Applying Fear. Add the rolled Fear to the character's current total. Each point of Fear removes one die from Attribute-based Pools, including Martial Attack, Spell Casting, Skill, Attribute and Ritual Checks. Apply this flat reduction before percentage Health Penalties. The final Pool can reach 0 dice; a Fear Check made with 0 dice falls in the 0-7 band and gains +2 Fear. Keep, Damage Dice, Death Checks and MR-based Initiative Dice retain their normal values.

Recovery. Fear continues across scenes and combats. A Safe Haven Rest returns Fear to 0. Healing, Cleanse, Night Rest and Day of Rest resolve their own listed effects, leaving the Fear total in place.

Check procedure. A Fear Check uses Resolve k1 and the fixed table. Skill Points and Raises are not part of this check; existing Mental Restrictions apply according to their own rules.

::

Fear Check Examples

Example — Sudden horror: A character rolls Resolve k1 and keeps a 7. The result is below 8, so they gain 2 Fear.

Example — Unsettling revelation: Another character rolls Resolve k1 and keeps 15. The result falls within 8–15, so they gain 1 Fear.

Example — Holding steady: A third character keeps 16 (or more) and gains 0 Fear. The same bands apply whether the event was ordinary or supernatural; the GM does not select an alternate Fear TN.

Boundary results: 7 → +2, 8 → +1, 15 → +1, 16 → +0.

Accumulation: If a character begins the scene with Fear 2 and rolls an 8, they gain 1 Fear and now have Fear 3. With Resolve 8 and Fear 3, their Resolve-based Attribute Pool is 5 dice before any percentage Health Penalty. Fear remains until a Safe Haven Rest or an explicit future rule provides another way to remove it; the final Pool can reach 0 dice.

Special Effects Reference

Special Effects Reference

“Power leaves its mark — but every mark can be broken.”

This section summarizes all Special Effects by how they work mechanically.

Specials do not grant an automatic Attribute Check when applied.

If a Power hits or a Spell is successfully cast, its Specials apply.

Negative value-based Specials decay at the start of the affected creature's turn.

Cleanse and specific rules may reduce or remove Specials.

Global Rules

Effect Types
Most entries fall into one of these types:

  • Diminishing (X→0):
    The effect has a stack value X. Reapplying the same effect usually adds stacks. At the start of the target’s turn, the effect ticks (if it has a Tick), then decays by 1.

  • Timed:
    The effect lasts for a listed duration (1 Round, MR Rounds, etc.), then ends.
    Timed effects do not stack unless an entry explicitly says otherwise. Reapplying them refreshes duration and keeps the higher X.

  • Until Broken / Until Used:
    The effect lasts until its listed break condition is met, or until its uses are spent.
    These effects do not stack unless an entry explicitly says otherwise.

  • Instant:
    The effect resolves immediately and does not persist unless the entry says otherwise.

Special Application Limit

A creature can receive a maximum of:

4 × its Mastery Rank

new points of the same Diminishing Special during a single Round.

For a numeric Diminishing Special, determine the new points applied in this order: printed Special value, successful Raise Special Increase, eligible Intellect Stone Special Boost, eligible Passive: Special Amplification on the owner's attack-delivered Special, target Vulnerability, target Special Negation, then the target's remaining per-Round application allowance. If that allowance is already exhausted, the newly applied amount is 0. Apply the surviving amount to stored stacks. Special Aura modifies an existing stack's effective value only while in range; it is not a new application.

This limit counts all applications of that Special from all sources combined. Any amount beyond this limit is ignored. This is an application limit, not a maximum stack value. Special points already present from previous Rounds do not count against the limit.

Natural Special Recovery

At the start of its Turn, after resolving all Ticks, a creature reduces one or more negative Diminishing Specials currently affecting it by a total amount equal to its Mastery Rank. The creature chooses freely how to distribute this reduction among its negative Diminishing Specials. If a Special reaches 0, it ends. Any unused reduction is lost.

Root is excluded from Natural Special Recovery. Root follows its own Until Broken recovery rule instead.

Cleanse(X)

Choose one creature. Remove up to X total points from one or more ongoing negative Specials affecting that creature that list Cleanse: Yes.

You may distribute the Cleanse value freely between those eligible Specials. If a Special reaches 0, it ends. Any unused Cleanse value is lost.

Single-focus Cleanse: Cleanse only reduces eligible negative Specials. It does not grant Damage, Armor, Evade, Speed, Healing, Restoration, Temporary HP, or Absorption Stones. A character needs separate legal Powers for any such additional effects.

Diminishing Effects

Diminishing (X→0):
Reapplying the same effect adds stacks (X → X + Y) unless stated otherwise.
At the start of the affected creature’s turn, resolve the effect’s Tick (if any), then reduce X by 1 (X → X−1, minimum 0).
If X reaches 0, the effect ends.

Effect What It Does Stacking Cleanse
Challenge(X) Challenge is bound to the creature that applied it. Attack Pools for attacks that do not include that creature as a target are reduced by X (minimum 0 dice). Same source only Yes
Corrode(X) Your Armor is reduced by X. Yes Yes
Disoriented(X) Your Attack Dice and all dice pools used to notice, locate, track, or identify something are reduced by X (minimum 0 dice). Yes Yes
Expose(X) Your Evade is reduced by X. Yes Yes

Mark applied by this same hit becomes usable on the next hit. Yes Yes
Ruin(X) At Tick, take X damage. Yes Yes
Slow(X) Each point reduces Speed by 1 m, minimum 0 m. At the start-of-Turn Tick, if Speed is 0 m or voluntary movement is prevented by another effect, take X damage, ignoring Armor. Otherwise, Slow deals no damage. Resolve before Natural Special Recovery and decay. Yes Yes
Soulburn(X) All dice pools based on Wits, Influence, or Resolve are reduced by X (minimum 0 dice). Yes Yes

Timed and Fixed Control Effects

Timed effects do not stack unless explicitly stated otherwise.
Reapplying a Timed effect refreshes its duration. If it has a numeric value, keep the higher X.
Fixed Control effects are binary and never gain an X-value.

Effect What It Does Duration Stacking Cleanse
Blight(X) While affected, all your Attribute-based dice pools have Disadvantage. X is the remaining number of your Turns; reduce it by 1 at the end of each Turn. X Turns No; reapplication refreshes to the higher remaining duration Yes
Brace(X) Your Speed becomes 0 m. While Braced, your Shield value is doubled for Armor calculation. At the end of each of your turns, reduce Brace by 1. Until X reaches 0 No No
Prone You are knocked down and helpless until you stand. Your normal Evade still applies. Spend 1 Attack Action to stand; then other actions and Reactions become available. Standing does not consume Movement. Until you stand No No

Until Broken / Until Used Effects

Critical is not a general Special. Critical(X) designates X qualifying Attack or Casting Pools to explode on 7–8 as defined in Core Terms, with the source determining the available combat or Round allowance. It may be granted through Passive: Critical, Active Buff: Critical, or Agility Ability: Crit; choose only one source per eligible roll. Artifact Stone Power Support may pre-fill named Ranks of the Crit Stone Ability, but it never grants Critical directly.

Effect What It Does Duration Stacking Cleanse
Bulwark(X) As a Reaction when hit by an attack you can perceive, reduce the attack’s final damage by 50% and consume 1 Bulwark. Until used Yes No
Immovable A wearer with Feet Artifact Base Value B: Immovable who declares it during Round Preparation has 0 m voluntary Movement, but cannot be forcibly displaced for that Round. This does not grant immunity to Prone or remove Evade. 1 Round No No
Root(X) Root has a minimum applied value of 2. Root stacks from all sources into one value and records the highest Mastery Rank among its contributing sources. While Root is above 0, your Speed is 0 m and you cannot move voluntarily. At the start of your Turn, reduce Root by your Mastery Rank. Spend 1 Attack Action or 1 Movement to make a Vitality Attribute Check against TN (8 × highest recorded source MR) − 2. On success, reduce Root by exactly 1, regardless of the margin of success. Clear the source MR when Root ends. Until broken Yes Yes

::

Instant Effects

Instant Specials resolve as part of the successful hit that delivered them.

They do not grant an automatic Attribute Check.

Effect What It Does Stacking Cleanse
Brutal Impact(X) Each damage die rolled counts as at least X. No No
Penetration(X) The attack ignores X Armor. No No
Precision(X) On hit, add +Xd8 bonus damage. No No
Push(X) Push the target X m immediately. No No
Pull(X) Pull the target X m immediately. No No

Stunned On application, the target loses 1 available Attack Action in the current Round. Resolve the Action loss immediately. No No

Support Effects

Effect What It Does Duration Stacking

If you need the full wording for an effect, including timing, stacking, and removal details, see the Appendix — Special Descriptions below.
